threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think a flat white costs under three quid and aren’t ready for the coffee shop line to wrap around the block.
Caught a guy in a tweed suit debating philosophy with a group of teens on the N35. Only in Brixton do deep thoughts happen after midnight.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I found a random street party on a Tuesday night, complete with a makeshift dance floor made from crates. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, it's not unusual to see a guy in a beret playing the accordion next to a food truck selling vegan döner. Only in Berlin!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their reaction to a BART delay—just a sigh and a 'What’s new?' while tourists panic.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo calmly read a book on the 47, surrounded by rush hour chaos and a guy juggling. Only in the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia’s plazas are quiet hideaways, but locals know they’re actually just loud gathering spots for evening 'botellóns'.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still flinch when the metro doors close unexpectedly. The locals just know to step aside and let the chaos flow.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it ‘Stokey’ instead of the proper ‘Stoke Newington’ like the locals do. Even the pigeons seem to side-eye you for that.
Last night on the 196, a guy in a full tuxedo berated the driver for being late. Turns out he was late for a wedding he’d apparently just crashed.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I spotted a pigeon stealing a döner from a street vendor and the vendor just laughed. That’s Neukölln for you—chaotic charm.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a döner shop charging more for vegan options than the classic lamb. Just Berlin things, I guess!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they know to jump off the bus a stop early when BART suffers yet another meltdown. It's like a survival instinct here.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a bus driver calmly explaining route changes to a lost tourist, while a jazz trio played a lively tune on the corner. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the locals love paella; in Gràcia, you'll find far more people loyal to their calçots and a good romesco.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they pause at every corner, checking their phones instead of just enjoying the architecture around them.
